constraints: Three seeded directives selected from six authored contracts.
Progress, timeout, reward, and result state are owned by the local Node host.
Bounded night history, total score, best result, cleared acts, round seed, and next-Setlist preview are owned by the runtime host; aborting a round does not consume it.
The host deterministically selects OPENING, RECONNECT, LOCK-IN, or HEADLINER plans from the latest bounded authoritative receipt; adapted act kinds are fixed before the next round starts.
Every plan carries a stable mode, title, short cue, source round, full reason, and exact act kinds; no difficulty or objective change is hidden from the room.
Restored pre-cue checkpoints are normalized into the current Conductor contract without losing result state, show history, the completed-round receipt, or the next adapted plan.
The shared lobby/result and 390x844 controller expose the same RECONNECT SET reason, cue, Round 2 identity, and CALL & RESPONSE / PASS THE MIC / CHAIN REACTION plan.
Only current human players may cast or replace a next-round signal vote; a live AI attempt returned HTTP 403 without changing revision, votes, or plan.
The server counts one replaceable vote per eligible human, resolves ties with the stable TOGETHER / BOLD / FLOW order, and maps the winner to one exact authored three-act plan.
The bounded schema targets exactly the next unplayed round, survives fresh-process checkpoint recovery, is copied into the consumed Conductor receipt, and rolls forward only after round completion.

The 390x844 human controller exposes three accessible vote buttons and current tally; the 1280x720 shared lobby exposes the winning signal, vote count, transparent reason, and exact next plan. AI controllers do not receive voting authority.
Support AI idle decisions outside active play no longer advance action sequences or fill the bounded input ledger with rejected synthetic actions.
Every set contains a human-required act; support AI cannot clear the full setlist alone.
Managed browser verification passed at 1280x720 in lobby, active play, results, replay, and reset recovery.
Managed portrait-browser verification passed at 390x844 with the directive and all touch controls visible without overflow.
Shared lobby, active directive, receipt, replay, reset recovery, and portrait controller expose the same authoritative show/round identity and next plan.
The shared display exposes RECONNECTING then HOST RESTORED, while seat observation gives controllers an explicit REJOINED cue; both return to the same authoritative show identity.
The local host writes a size-limited schema envelope through same-directory temporary write, fsync, and atomic rename; checkpoints are roster-bound and expire after 30 minutes by default.
A same-host, same-roster runtime relaunch restores lobby, countdown, active, or result state; live deadlines are rebased so downtime does not consume the round. This is not host migration.
Accepted sequence counters survive restart, stale sequences remain rejected, and held movement/pulse buffers restore neutral to prevent duplicated or stuck input.
A completed-show summary is projected only from server-owned Show Memory and includes the bounded last round, next plan, totals, best result, and cleared acts.

Managed runtimes can POST a capped result envelope only to the configured loopback Game Hub /game/end route; sender, receiver, stored result, Hub lobby state, and stopped child were observed for one managed session.

A successful explicit handback retires the show checkpoint before Game Hub ends the child; the next managed launch was a fresh lobby with zero history and totals. Callback failure re-enables checkpoint persistence.
After at least one completed round, the shared display exposes a two-step Return to Game Hub action and a visible SHOW SAVED transition; the action is hidden for a fresh show.
Determinism, rotation, human gating, reward, and result closure are covered.
HTTP state and seat observation expose the authoritative setlist.
Core and HTTP tests prove deterministic seed advancement, changed directives, bounded history, persistent totals, and abort-safe replay identity.
A separate-process HTTP test proves restore with paused time, neutral input, sequence continuity, explicit New Show reset, and safe fallbacks for corrupt, expired, and roster-mismatched checkpoints.
A fake loopback receiver plus runtime HTTP test proves availability/refusal rules, exact receiver payload, single-send behavior, checkpoint retirement, and fresh relaunch.
Core, HTTP, recovery, and handback tests cover deterministic plan modes, exact adapted act kinds, cross-process persistence, legacy-state migration, receipt transport, and idle-AI no-op behavior.

Core, HTTP, and fresh-process recovery tests cover authorization, validation, idempotence, vote replacement, deterministic ties, exact plan application, round consumption, receipt storage, and checkpoint persistence.
One complete managed round visibly rotated all three acts, cleared one act, awarded 240 bonus points, rendered a 1/3 receipt, replayed into countdown, and recovered to a clean lobby.
Managed Round 1 at seed 12026 visibly previewed and replayed into the exact changed Round 2 at seed 12027 on desktop and portrait surfaces; reset preserved history and the unconsumed Round 2 plan.

A managed Game Hub stop/start visibly traversed RECONNECTING to HOST RESTORED and recovered the exact active round identity, score, revision, clock, player position, Setlist act, and input sequence; controller observation rendered REJOINED.
The managed lobby visibly exposed Return to Game Hub, a non-destructive confirmation state, and SHOW SAVED · RETURNING before the callback stopped the runtime.
A full managed opening round produced a receipt-driven RECONNECT SET; shared result/lobby and portrait result/active states visibly exposed its reason and exact plan with measured no-overflow fit.

In managed session session-1785246383789, Mike selected BOLD on the portrait controller; shared lobby and both active surfaces visibly rendered the exact HUMAN SPOTLIGHT / PASS THE MIC / RIDE THE STATIC plan with zero measured overflow and zero console warnings/errors.
